title: Punk Graphics — An idea turns into a system

scenes.title: Headline paste-up
scenes.purpose: Build the ransom-note headline line by line on torn black paper, each line larger than the last.
visuals: cool grey engineering graph paper with toner speckle (stationary)
torn black strip with a white fibre rim
mixed-font cutout letter tiles in paper white, protest red and black
torn white label reading INTO A SYSTEM
red halftone torn sheet slapped on the right

beats.development: The black torn strip slaps down off-angle, then the AN IDEA tiles are pasted one at a time with small rotation errors.
Larger TURNS tiles are pasted, the INTO A SYSTEM label lands with tape, and the halftone sheet slaps on the right side.

scenes.title: The system gets inked
scenes.purpose: The idea becomes a connected system: a red hub sticker, hand-inked spokes, node stickers, then node-to-node links.
visuals: red hub die-cut sticker with a white rim
white node stickers with red X marks landing as each spoke arrives
HUD chips counting NODES and LINKS

beats.development: The hub pops on and five spokes ink outward one after another; each node sticker lands as its line arrives, and the NODES counter climbs to 06.
Thinner ring lines join neighbouring nodes so the network no longer depends only on the centre. LINKS reaches 10.

scenes.title: Punchline and hold
scenes.purpose: Land the handwritten caption and the CONNECTED stamp, then hold the finished collage for reading.
visuals: torn caption scrap with handwritten line and red marker underline
white scrap with distressed red CONNECTED rubber stamp

beats.development: The caption scrap settles and the marker underline is drawn, the stamp scrap lands, and CONNECTED is stamped in stepped motion.
Everything is settled and fully legible for a reading hold.

findings: Each line of the headline is readable as soon as it is pasted, from about 1.0s onward.
Attention moves from left to right: headline, then network, then the punchline stamp. The caption and stamp overlap briefly at the end.
All motion ends by 2.6s, so the composition is settled before 2.7s.
justifiedHolds: 2.6–3.0s: a still hold so the complete collage and the CONNECTED stamp can be read.

notes: Background was chosen for this scene: cool grey engineering graph paper (#E2E6E9) instead of the earlier warm #EFE9D9 swatch, following the source review's engineering-paper option. Ink #171717, the single print accent #C63A3A and paper stock #F4F2EC are kept.

Source subject, lettering, characters and branding were not copied. Only the construction roles were taken: grid substrate, ransom tiles, one print accent, halftone, sticker rims, stamp punchline and HUD chips.
